newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open down $50 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open down $50 a tonne.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $50 a tonne lower on Thursday as the market is expected to follow through on sharp losses made Wednesday, traders said.
New York cocoa futures fell to 10-day lows as the speculators, who carried the market to nine-year highs, liquidated recently acquired long positions.
September ended $71 lower at $1,614, the weakest close since June 20.
An estimated 13,515 lots changed hands on the day.

Cocoa prices have lost more than five percent of their value in the past two days in a technical correction. News of favorable growing conditions in the Ivory Coast for the 1997/98 crop has added some light fundamental pressure.
CSCE September cocoa will need to hold above $1,580 to prevent another fund-linked selloff, analysts said.

London cocoa futures were trading down sharply on Wednesday in the wake of losses in New York. At the midday break, LIFFE July cocoa stood 43 stg lower at 1,050 stg, having broken the key support level of 1,000 stg. September stood 39 stg lower at 1,070 stg.
